title: FIM is standard in code pretraining
text: Seven of the reports describe fill-in-the-middle training. StarCoder2 applies it to 50% of repositories and then to each file chunk with 50% probability, DeepSeek-Coder and DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (16B only) use a 0.5 rate, Code Llama uses 0.9, and Seed-Coder uses 0.5 in regular pretraining and 0.1 in continued pretraining.

title: Context is extended in a short stage after the base run
text: Code Llama, DeepSeek-Coder, StarCoder2, Qwen2.5-Coder and SmolLM3 grow context in a separate stage that uses a small share of the budget, for example StarCoder2's 200B tokens at 16,384 or SmolLM3's two 50B-token stages to 32k and 64k. DeepSeek-Coder-V2 reaches 128K in two steps of 1000 training steps each, at 32K and then 128K.

title: Many recipes start from an existing model
text: Code Llama (500B tokens on Llama 2), DeepSeek-Coder-V2 (6T tokens from a DeepSeek-V2 checkpoint), Qwen2.5-Coder (5.5T tokens on Qwen2.5) and Kimi-Dev (about 150B mid-training tokens on Qwen2.5-72B-Base) all continue from earlier weights. Only Code Llama reports the comparison: an identical 7B model trained from scratch on the same data needed about 240B more tokens to match its loss.

title: Synthetic data is kept only if it executes
text: Code Llama keeps the first of ten sampled solutions that passes generated unit tests, Qwen2.5-Coder keeps synthetic pretraining code only if an executor ran it, Seed-Coder and OpenCoder verify synthetic instruction data in a sandbox or with test cases, and Olmo 3 keeps (problem, solution, tests) triplets whose solutions pass more than 80% of tests. OpenCodeReasoning is the counterexample: it found execution filtering lowered benchmark accuracy and preferred instruction diversity.

title: RL rewards for code are binary pass or fail on tests
text: DeepCoder, AceReason-Nemotron, Skywork-OR1, DeepSWE-Preview and Kimi-Dev all use a 0 or 1 outcome reward, and DeepCoder says it avoids K-of-N partial credit because it can lead to reward hacking. AceReason and DeepCoder reward code only if it passes all tests, and Kimi-Dev requires the patch to pass all ground-truth unit tests.

title: RL prompts are filtered to a difficulty band
text: Skywork-OR1 removes prompts the base model always or never solves, AceReason scores difficulty with DeepSeek-R1-671B and drops unsolved problems, Kimi-Dev discards prompts with pass@16 of 0 and re-adds them later, and Seed-Coder's reasoning run filters problems with correctness above 87.5%. Skywork-OR1 and Kimi-Dev state that zero-advantage groups and prompts with pass@16 of 0 do not contribute to the loss.

title: Reasoning RL drops the KL term and grows context in stages
text: DeepCoder, DeepSWE, Seed-Coder, Skywork-OR1 and AceReason remove or zero the KL loss, and DeepCoder, DeepSWE and Seed-Coder also use DAPO-style changes such as clip high or overlong filtering. AceReason extends response length from 8K to 32K in stages, Skywork-OR1 uses multi-stage context growth, and DeepCoder lengthens from 16K to 32K.

title: A late phase of higher-quality data closes pretraining
text: Granite Code ends with 500B tokens of 80% code and 20% language data after 3T to 4T code-only tokens, OpenCoder anneals on 100B tokens that include synthetic code textbooks and algorithmic data, and SmolLM3 raises code from 12% to 24% in its last decay phase. Seed-Coder and Olmo 3 likewise switch to high-quality and task data in continued pretraining and midtraining.
